news: New Chairman Shawn Pelsinger's election became effective today (July 24, 2026), coinciding with the annual shareholder meeting; he succeeds Carl Albert, who moves to Chairman Emeritus/advisor.
Debt refinancing cut convertible notes from ~$47M to $16.9M and added a $30M term loan plus a $21.6M aircraft-backed facility, easing near-term liquidity.
Wheels Up signed as launch customer for Enterprise BrokerOS (up to $12M subscription revenue); expanded Palantir SurfOS partnership. Still deeply unprofitable (margin under -100%, current ratio 0.2).
FY2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results call confirmed for Monday, July 27, 2026 at 5:00pm ET (3 days away); focus will be data-center utilization, capex, and funding plans.
Nvidia's exit from its equity stake in Applied Digital has weighed on sentiment; stock down ~44% over the trailing month on AI-capex and semiconductor-volatility concerns.
Wall Street stays Strong Buy despite the drawdown: 16 analysts, median target $70.56 (~150% implied upside from current price).
Board added Andreas Lieber (ex-Uber/Postmates) as director, effective June 22, 2026.
Expanding beyond food delivery: NoScrubs laundry pilot launched in select LA neighborhoods; 'Moving Canvas' robot-as-public-art program debuted at Cannes Lions.
Analyst consensus remains Buy (8 analysts, $18.45 target) despite the stock down sharply YTD and continued net losses.
FDA announced plans to take 'decisive steps' against compounded GLP-1 products following its July 23-24 peptide-compounding panel; stock fell 9.2% today, its largest single-day move in the book.

HIMS separately announced a strategic shift for its US weight-loss business: it will stop advertising compounded GLP-1s and lean on FDA-approved medications plus limited compounded semaglutide via its Novo Nordisk partnership.
CFO sold ~$229K in shares over a 3-day slide ahead of the FDA meeting. Q2 2026 earnings due August 10, 2026.
Reported Q2 FY26 earnings July 22, 2026: beat on both lines (EPS $0.90 vs. $0.76 est.; revenue +24% YoY) and raised full-year guidance.
Stock initially sold off into the print (already down hard YTD) but rallied 6.1% today as the beat gets digested; RSI recovering from oversold territory (36.5).
New joint AI-powered cybersecurity offering launched with Accenture; AI-native platform adoption (Now Assist, Autonomous Workforce) cited as the key growth driver.
Q4 FY26 earnings due July 29, 2026 (5 days away); consensus EPS $4.23, following six straight quarters of beats.
S&P downgraded credit rating to BBB- on rising AI-data-center debt; stock remains far off its September 2025 peak despite record FY26 results (cloud revenue +47%, cloud infrastructure +93%).
$0.50/share quarterly dividend paid July 24, 2026.
RSI at 29.99 keeps ORCL just under the oversold line for a fourth straight session; market still questioning whether the $638B AI backlog converts to cash fast enough to service the debt load.

A securities-fraud class action was filed alleging an anticompetitive Zillow-Redfin agreement; lead-plaintiff deadline is August 10, 2026. Shares fell as much as ~16% on the initial allegation and remain well off recent highs despite today's 3.4% bounce.
Jefferies cut its price target to $60 (from $75) on July 14 but maintained a Buy rating.
